subject: Your sizing code has two risk floors and they disagree - which one did you mean?
body:
Eighth version. One thing in here needs a decision from you.

BOARD: 26 of 46 criteria now have an automated checker, 11 of them MET. This morning it was 16 of a
wrongly-remembered 40, with 7 MET.

Newly earned: C5.6 (every sizing layer logs its operand and result -- 15 layers, all traced, and I
have named in the output that the log sits behind a rate-limit gate so it does not fire on every
trade). C5.7 is not met: three hardcoded numbers survive in the risk chain.

THE ONE THAT NEEDS YOU.

Your sizing code has two risk floors nineteen lines apart, and they disagree.

    line 58900   baseRiskPercent = MathMax(MinRiskPercent, MathMin(MaxRiskPercent, ...))
    line 58919   baseRiskPercent = MathMax(0.5, MathMin(_ceoRiskCap, baseRiskPercent))

MinRiskPercent is an input, set to 1.5%, and its comment says "Minimum risk floor -- 0.01 lot micro
viability". The second line hardcodes 0.5 instead, and it runs AFTER the first, so it wins.

And it is reachable, not theoretical: g_CEO_RiskCeiling is set to MathMax(0.5, 2.0 - depth*1.5) as
the competence score falls, then halved again with the same 0.5 floor. So when the system is doing
badly, risk goes to a third of the minimum you declared.

There are two honest readings and I am not going to pick between them for you:

  IT IS CORRECT. De-risking hard when the evidence weakens is exactly what your own C8.3 criterion
  asks the system to do. This is that behaviour working, and MinRiskPercent is a floor for normal
  operation rather than for a system in trouble.

  IT IS A BUG. The comment on MinRiskPercent says the floor is there for lot-size viability. If
  0.5% risk produces a position below the broker's minimum lot, the order does not get smaller --
  it gets rejected. The de-risking would then be silently turning into no trading at all.

Which one it is depends on your account size and the broker's minimum lot, which I can compute if
you tell me, or you can just say which floor you meant. It is a one-word change either way (0.5 ->
MinRiskPercent, or a comment saying the override is deliberate). I have not touched it -- run 5 is
live and the deploy rule stands.

Two small things I caught in my own checker before publishing, since I have been telling you when
these happen: it double-counted one violation (4 instead of 3), and it initially blamed the wrong
line for the floor conflict -- line 58692 uses `*=`, so its 0.70 bounds a multiplier and is not a
risk floor at all. Both fixed before the number reached you.

Run 5 is at 98% of its calibration budget and skipping the last two stages on the clock, so it
should finish shortly. That is the third calibration C6.3/C6.4 need.
